data.heading: HTML5 Canvas vs SVG Drawing
HTML5 Canvas
items: Pixel-based, incredibly fast for thousands of objects.
Requires manual redraw loops for animation.
No DOM nodes, harder to attach events.
Best for particles, complex shaders, and games.

data.heading: SVG Drawing
items: Native DOM integration for CSS styling and events.
Can be sluggish with too many complex paths.
Perfect for charts, graphs, and UI components.

data.speakerNotes: A classic debate for UI engineers. We use SVG for structural clarity and Canvas for high-performance visual effects.

questions.question: What is the primary risk of using highly stylized, cinematic interfaces in functional applications?
options: They require too much server bandwidth.
They are impossible to build with standard web technologies.
They can prioritize aesthetics over readability and user efficiency.
They cause hardware damage to older monitors.
questions.explanation: While beautiful, excessive glows, low contrast, and complex animations can fatigue users and obscure critical data.

data.heading: Cinematic Wrap-Up
items: Cinematic UI elevates the user experience through depth and motion.
Balance aesthetics with usability; don't let design obscure data.
Leverage modern CSS (OKLCH, filters) for performant visual effects.
Use spring physics for organic, satisfying interactions.
